title: AI-assisted drone helps rescuers find two overdue hikers
date_precision: Reported overdue June 23, 2026. Exact rescue date unreported. Official account published June 25, 2026.
location: Dead Horse Gap walking track, near Jindabyne, New South Wales, Australia
system: Fire and Rescue NSW drone with AI detection software and thermal camera. Model and vendor not identified.
observed_outcome: Both hikers were located and guided to safety.
ai_contribution: The agency attributes initial identification in the bush to the drone's AI software. Thermal imaging confirmed the find.
human_contribution: The drone operator confirmed the find using thermal imagery and used a spotlight to guide Police and State Emergency Service rescuers. The hikers also signaled with a phone light.
evidence_type: Official operational report. No independent causal evaluation.
evidence_supports: A first-party operational account describes identification, confirmation, and rescue.
limitations: The report does not isolate AI's contribution from thermal imaging, the hikers' signal, or rescuers. It does not establish injuries or deaths avoided, or time saved.
tradeoffs: No adverse effects are reported. Costs, surveillance implications, and false detections are not evaluated.
replication_hypothesis: Test whether trained operators, effective imaging, ground-team coordination, and clear confirmation procedures enable similar rescues.

sources.title: Fire and Rescue NSW drone team locates missing hikers using AI technology

benefit_summary: Two overdue hikers were found and guided to safety during an AI-assisted drone search.
stakeholder_detail: The two hikers are the reported direct beneficiaries. Rescuers are contributing practitioners. A separate benefit to their workload or safety is not established.

evidence_basis.reported_by: Fire and Rescue NSW, an agency participating in the rescue
evidence_basis.outcome_documentation: The agency describes identification, confirmation, ground-team coordination, and return to safety.
evidence_basis.verification_limit: No independent event verification or comparative causal evaluation is supplied.

ai_attribution: The agency reports that AI software identified the hikers. Thermal imaging, the hikers' phone light, and human rescuers also contributed.
editorial_classification_note: Rescue is the observed benefit. Do not infer lives saved, injuries avoided, or search time saved.
